To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the unlicensed bands can be used to offload a significant fraction of cellular traffic, 2) the use of the licensed bands for D2D communication can be beneficial for both cellular and unlicensed traffic offloading, 3) the use of D2D communication for offloading cellular traffic is beneficial for both cellular operators and WiFi providers, and 4) the use of unlicensed bands can significantly reduce the need for additional CAPEX investment to deploy picocells.
The performance of a cellular network with D2D offloading is highly dependent on the network configuration and the D2D offload strategy.

the use of D2D connections in the context of cellular offloading has the potential to provide substantial benefits in terms of network load reduction, but the actual gains will vary depending on a number of factors, including the number of concurrent cellular and WiFi links, the amount of traffic offloaded to D2D, the number of D2D links, the traffic distribution between cellular and D2D, and the number of users involved in each D2D link.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of D2D communications to offload cellular traffic onto WiFi connections in order to reduce the load on cellular networks and improve user experience.
the design and implementation of a system that enables cellular traffic offloading to D2D connections in the unlicensed band.

the design of algorithms for the optimal offloading of cellular traffic onto D2D connections in a way that maximizes the overall system throughput, while ensuring that the cellular traffic demand is met and the cellular and D2D connections are interference-free.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cellular traffic offloading is an effective way to increase network capacity, but the benefits are limited to the unlicensed spectrum.

the use of unlicensed bands in the near future will be a very important factor for the evolution of mobile networks, as they are the only way to cope with the increasing demand for mobile data traffic.

cellular traffic offloading onto D2D links in the unlicensed bands can be an efficient way of reducing network congestion, and that this can be done without any additional investment in base station equipment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel D2D offloading scheme that can be used to offload cellular traffic to unlicensed WiFi connections.

we have shown that it is possible to offload a substantial portion of the cellular traffic onto D2D connections, while still guaranteeing that the cellular network is able to deliver a minimum quality of experience to all users.
we have shown how to use D2D communications to offload cellular traffic, and how this offloading process can be managed in a way that is both efficient and robust to mobility and channel variations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of unlicensed spectrum for offloading can be beneficial, even in cases where the cellular network is not congested.
, even with the limited spectrum resources of WiFi and LTE, it is possible to achieve a 50% offloading ratio, which is a significant gain for operators.

, while D2D traffic offloading is not a panacea for the cellular traffic problem, it can be used to reduce the load on the cellular infrastructure and thus delay the need to deploy additional base stations.
